criteria.rationale: The workflow follows the operative approval requirements, preserves the requested technical and nomination signoffs, and accurately reflects TechSol's authorized in-house role. Inspection covered all extracted paragraphs, gate-table rows, pricing rules, change exceptions and release instructions. The modular-price calculation is a proposed commercial rule, not unsupported historical pricing; quantities, units, validity and double-counting controls are specified without inventing values. No unsupported monetary thresholds, implementation dates, guaranteed savings or completed approvals are asserted. Fast-path reuse does not bypass price-change approvals, and release remains conditional on completed gates. The observable tool events show workspace listing and record reads, not external communications. The incomplete trace does not establish anything about unobserved actions.

criteria.rationale: The delivered Word-document extract substantively fulfills the first-level executive and technical workflow brief. It covers requirements, supplier assessment, RFQ and negotiation, nomination, baseline locking, post-nomination triage, compatible-module reuse, exception handling, mandatory price approvals and controlled release. The modular model includes all four requested cost-driver categories, commercial data fields, a configuration-price rule and a baseline-to-proposal cost bridge. Platform records, version-bound approvals, evidence retention, dashboards and implementation questions provide a usable foundation for TechSol without prescribing an unnecessary technology stack. Open governance and integration matters are presented as matters to confirm, not established facts. The holds are tied to missing impacts, unsupported assumptions or mandatory approvals rather than a blanket restart of sourcing. Native rendering and compliance with the requested 2–3-page limit remain separate, pending engineering checks; this judgment does not certify pagination, visual quality or human acceptance.
